Sam Torres: ran the multi-region failover + replay harness this morning (10:30 PT). TL;DR: primary->secondary fallback caused KV cache hit rate collapse and kernel selection mismatch under mixed-seq traffic. p99 token latency doubled in eu fallback and costs went up ~2x. full logs + repro attached.
Lena Zhou: can you paste the exact replay command and which model variants we used? also which kernel selection policy was active? @corey pls fyi.
Sam Torres: replay command we used:
```
./perf-runner replay --trace=traces/2026-02-12/fallback-run.json --concurrency=160 --region-src=us-west --region-dst=eu-west --model=redwood-open-1.5q --quant=8bit --kernel-policy=auto
```
Model variants: redwood-open-1.5q (gpu-optimized), redwood-open-1.5q-cpu-fallback, and a smaller redwood-1.2-llm for emergency fallback. Kernel policy=auto (selector picks kernel based on avg seq len and hardware tag).

Corey Patel: quick note from profiler: when requests fall back to eu-west we see a sudden jump in short-session requests (chat-like), avg_seq drops but P90 length still high -> selector chooses short-seq kernel for most batches, but long requests still arrive in same batch leading to kernel swap thrash. paste from perf sample below.

perf-bot: perf snapshot 1764528910-report:
```
scenario: primary->fallback drain
throughput: 1450 rps (target 1500)
kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.48
kernel_switch_rate: 0.17 (switches per 1000 tokens)
latency.tokens.p50: 12ms p95: 230ms p99: 980ms
cost.per_1k_tokens: $0.032 (baseline $0.017)
```

Maria Gomez: KV cache hit dropping to 48% is the big deal here. When we drain the region we spin up new serving pools in eu-west that don't have the warmed KV caches. Two things compound: (1) routing fallback sends a mix of prefixed+fresh sessions to same pool, invalidating prefix caching heuristics, and (2) the batching heuristic batches across session age which kills prefix affinity.

Lena Zhou: do we have an apples-to-apples comparison (same traffic replayed against warmed eu-west pool vs cold pool)? we need to separate kernel selection from cache warming effects.

Sam Torres: yes — ran two replays: (A) cold eu pool (fresh instances) and (B) warmed pool (pre-warmed with 1.2M tokens of trace). Results were different: warmed pool kv_hit 0.89 and p99 310ms; cold pool kv_hit 0.48 and p99 980ms. Kernel switch rate also fell to 0.03 on warmed.

Corey Patel: config snippet we used for the apples-to-apples run:
```yaml
batcher:
  max_batch_tokens: 4096
  max_batch_size: 64
  affinity_by_session_age: true
kernel_selector:
  policy: percentile-aware
  lookback_windows: [50,200,1000]
kv_cache:
  prewarm: true
  shard_policy: sticky_by_session
```
Note: percentile-aware is an experiment we pushed yesterday; in cold runs kernel_selector still used "auto" which favors avg seq len.

Maria Gomez: hypothesis: kernel_selector's use of average seq length leads to bad decisions for heavy-tailed seq distributions. We should try selecting kernel using a high percentile (p90) and also split long requests from short in the queue (queue-splitting) to avoid head-of-line blocking.

Lena Zhou: agreed. proposed immediate steps: (1) re-run apples-to-apples with kernel_selector.policy=p90 and queue-splitting enabled, (2) add a warmup stage to route a small fraction of sticky sessions to new region before full cutover, (3) add metrics to perf dashboard showing kv_hit by session_age bucket.

Sam Torres: I ran step (1) locally overnight with a 1h replay; early numbers look promising: kv_hit up to 0.53 (still below warm but better), kernel_switch_rate down to 0.06, p99 fell to ~520ms. Not perfect, but shows kernel selection fix helps even without full warming.

Corey Patel: for the queue-splitting patch I sketched: if batch contains > 15% long requests (len > 512), split them into a dedicated long-request batch and process separately. Pseudocode:
```
func maybeSplitBatch(batch):
  longReqs = filter(batch, req.seqLen > 512)
  if len(longReqs)/len(batch) > 0.15:
    return [batch - longReqs, longReqs]
  return [batch]
```
This reduced head-of-line blocking in sim.

perf-bot: scheduled: perf/replay-1764529123 (queue-split + p90-kernel) in eu-west (warm=false) starting in 15m. Link: https://perf.internal/replays/1764529123

Maria Gomez: two gotchas to keep in mind for the multi-region run: (A) routing policy currently does not pre-warm caches when shifting >30% traffic in 60s, so region-drain will be cold by design, (B) fallback model mapping sometimes selects the smaller model but without adjusting batch_size -> causes under-utilization and unexpected latency increases.

Lena Zhou: actionable owners: @corey will land kernel_selector p90 change + queue-splitting PR, @sam will add a warmup-step to the routing rollout (staged sticky sessions), @maria will add kv_hit session_age panels to console. Perf team to rerun apples-to-apples and attach final numbers.

Sam Torres: cool. I'll post the perf links and attach the failing sample traces here after the scheduled run completes :thumbsup:

Corey Patel: on it, creating PR now. will tag you both for review.

perf-bot: run complete 1764529123-summary:
kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.56
kernel_switch_rate: 0.04
latency.tokens.p99: 490ms
notes: queue-splitting + p90 selector reduced tail by ~48% vs cold baseline, cost down ~30% vs cold baseline.

Lena Zhou: perfect — looks like a combination of cache warming + kernel selection + queue-splitting is the fix. moving to follow-up doc for rollout playbook. Thanks everyone.
